topics.label: Introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system, contextualises its complexity, and sets the stage for the lecture.

topics.label: Fundamentals and architecture of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles of complement, including its general cascade architecture, naming conventions, and the central role of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three recognition pathways that initiate the complement cascade and drive the deposition of C3b to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the three primary effector outcomes driven by complement activation: opsonization, generic inflammation, and pathogen lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the mechanisms and regulatory proteins that keep complement activation in check to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators lead to distinct clinical disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies and mechanisms employed by pathogens, such as Staphylococcus aureus, to evade complement destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
